newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian wool prices seen weak this week.
newsitem.headline: Australian wool prices seen weak this week.

text.p: Australian wool prices are expected to remain weak this week, Wesfarmers Dalgety said.
Sales this week are in Sydney, Melbourne and Fremantle with 136,490 bales rostered for sale. This is 47 percent greater than originally rostered.

In Sydney there are 51,860 bales of mostly good topmaking styles from the western districts. In Melbourne there are 30,380 bales of best to good topmaking including some very stylish clips from Tasmania and in Fremantle there are 54,252 bales of good topmaking styles.
The eastern market indicator fell 47 cents to 706 a kg clean. There were no sales in Fremantle.
"Weakness is expected to continue this week, however, grower reaction to the downturn is anticipated to make this less severe, Wesfarmers said.

Last week's pass-in rate quickly escalated as prices began to fall which may further increase this week, helping to prevent the market from falling much lower. Another factor supporting an upturn is the three week recess approaching which will cause buyers to take stock to cover over the period and close the season at a stable level. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
